items.title: What's on This Page
items.why:
A draft routine for Erica from your answers: strength and tone, new to training, 3 days a week, about 20 minutes.

1. The weekly plan
2. Workouts A and B
3. How it gets harder
4. The vest, Ab wheel and other pieces
5. How it looks in the app
6. Setup and publishing

Nothing is built yet. The Home and workout pictures are mock-ups on the real app; the exercise pictures are the app as it is today.

Which exercises, and their order, are my judgement. Amounts and safety come from the sources named on each card.

items.title: The Week
items.why:
Three days with a day off between, such as Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The workouts take turns:

Week 1: A, B, A
Week 2: B, A, B

Every workout covers the whole body, so a missed day never skips a muscle group. The app offers whichever is next, with no fixed days.

Sources: CDC says at least 2 strength days a week working all major muscle groups. Harvard Health says muscles need at least 48 hours between sessions.

items.title: Workout A
items.why:
Chair squat, no weight
Knee push-up
Bent-over dumbbell row, 5 lb each hand
Glute bridge
Side-lying leg lift, each side, no ankle weight at first
Dead bug

All six are rated Beginner in the app. One set of 8 to 12 reps each (CDC). Side exercises get 8 to 12 on each side.

items.title: Workout B
items.why:
Dumbbell Romanian deadlift, 5 lb each hand
Dumbbell floor press, 5 lb each hand
Dumbbell shoulder press, 5 lb each hand
Bent-over dumbbell row, 5 lb each hand
Slider reverse lunge, each side, holding a chair
Bird dog, each side

The row is in both on purpose, so the upper back is worked every time.

Harvard Health suggests starting with no weight or very light weight; 5 lb is the lightest your dumbbells make.

items.title: Dumbbells or Kettlebell for the Deadlift
items.why: Your kettlebells are 15 lb each. Two 5 lb dumbbells are 10 lb in total, so they're the lighter start, and the weight doesn't come up from the floor.

options.label: Dumbbells first
options.desc: The kettlebell can be swapped in later.

items.title: Warm-Up
items.why:
Harvard Health says to warm up and cool down for 5 to 10 minutes, and that walking is fine. The NHS warm-up takes at least 6 minutes, starting with marching on the spot.

My estimate with the 6 exercises at one set: about 15 to 20 minutes including a 5 minute walk. At two sets: about 25 to 30, or more. I haven't timed either.

options.label: One line on the card
options.desc: "Warm up first: walk for 5 to 10 minutes."

items.title: How It Gets Harder
items.why:
The app's Starter rule today: 12 reps on every exercise, two workouts in a row, and it offers another set. After 3 sets it offers timed circuits.

For Erica's routine I'd change the end: stay at 2 sets, because 3 would run well past 20 minutes. After that it suggests one step up at a time, such as 5 to 10 lb, or adding the ankle weight.

One limit: with even ends your dumbbells go 5, 10, 15. Harvard Health suggests adding only 1 to 2 lb at a time for arms, so going 5 to 10 is a big jump. The 2 sets come first, and the app won't push the heavier weight on arm exercises.

options.label: Same as Starter Workouts
options.desc: Up to 3 sets, then timed circuits.

options.label: 1 set, then 2, plus 7.5 and 12.5 lb
options.desc: Different plates on each end, for Erica only. Changes your earlier pick of even ends only.

items.title: Weighted Vest
items.why:
Not in A or B at the start. A separate walk on a day off would fit best.

Harvard Health: no more than 10% of body weight, so the 12 lb vest suits someone of 120 lb or more. Henry Ford Health suggests starting at 3% or less. I'm not assuming Erica's weight; the app knows it only if Erica enters it.

options.label: Plain walks; vest is in the library
Add one vest walk a week
options.desc: With the weight rule shown next to it.

items.title: Ab Wheel, Medicine Balls, Perfect Pushups
items.why:
The app's only medicine ball exercise is a slam (Intermediate), and the Ab wheel is also above Beginner. They stay in the library for later, as do the other slider exercises.

The Perfect Pushup handles could replace the knee push-up on the floor.

options.label: Use Perfect Pushups, from the knees

items.title: Home Card
items.why: What Erica sees on Home. The link under the button switches to the other workout. Sources stay at the bottom, as now.

options.label: List with A and B buttons

items.title: List on a Phone
items.why: The list makes the card taller. On a 393 x 852 screen Start Workout still shows without scrolling. Workout B is taller, since two names wrap; its picture is the card alone.

items.title: During the Workout
items.why: The same Starter screen: big counter, no timer, rest as long as needed. The new parts: the workout's name on top, the amount under the exercise, and the weight already set.

items.title: Erica's Setup Questions
items.why: You picked earlier that Erica chooses a goal in setup. With a routine ready, I'd fill in the answers you just gave me: new to it, strength, 3 days. Erica can change any of them. The health question is still asked, and a Yes still holds workouts until a doctor's OK.

options.label: Fill in, Erica can change them
